body:
CANDIDATE for the scout's RecallSignature audit, findings 1 and 4: d4443ff on branch m1/route-honesty, parent current main. Five files: align/signature.scala, SignatureSuite, WorkedExampleSuite (assertion updates), embed-bench report.scala + LeakageSuite (ClockPanel carries the Options). signature.scala is under my live reservation rv-01M16016CVXSHR7MM6DJCQERHB.

FINDING 1 - and the detail I want on the record is that OUR OWN CODE ALREADY KNEW. `ordered(...)` returns None when no step carries directional mass; it is written correctly. The caller then did `.getOrElse(1.0)` and published PERFECT FORWARD CHRONOLOGY for a recall we could not place at all. The honest abstention existed and was discarded one line later. Same for backwardMean, which divided by max(1, steps.size) and so reported 0.0 - "this person never moved backwards" - for a recall with no comparable transition at all. Both are Option now.

That pattern is worth naming because it is not the same as forgetting to handle a case: the uncertainty was COMPUTED, then thrown away at the boundary. If we are auditing for this class, `.getOrElse` on a freshly-computed Option is a high-yield grep, and I would suggest the scout add it to the sweep - it is a different signature from "never modelled the missing case".

FINDING 4 - SignatureProjection now returns Either[ProjectionError, Double]. Two failure modes were previously silent zeros: a weight naming a component that does not exist DELETED THAT DIMENSION of the score (a typo cost you a whole term and nothing said so), and a component we did not measure was scored 0.0 - worst possible for a coverage-like quantity, best possible under a negative weight. Both are now named errors: UnknownComponent and MissingComponent, each carrying the component name.

MUTATION PROOFS, four, each applied alone and reverted, and one of them taught me something:
S1 unknown component silently dropped -> the typo test FAILS.
S2 missing component scored 0.0 -> the abstention test FAILS.
S3 restore .getOrElse(1.0) -> FAILS, but ONLY after I added the right test. My first attempt at S3 SURVIVED, because every existing fixture has directional mass, so the default never fired. That is the third time tonight a mutant survived for a reason unrelated to the code, and the first time the reason was that MY TEST CORPUS COULD NOT REACH THE BRANCH. I added a recall with no comparable transition at all and it fails properly.
S4 restore the max(1, size) division -> FAILS on the same new test.

I did findings 1 and 4 together rather than splitting them because they are the same file and the same defect, and a half-fixed file would have left the projection erasing the very Options I had just introduced - the fix for 1 would have made 4 strictly worse. If you would rather have them as separate landings, say so and I will split the commit.

NOT DONE, deliberately, and they are the scout's findings 2 and 3: the fidelity 0.5 cliff, specificity renormalizing arbitrarily small source residue, and compression/coherence promoting conditional residue. Those are estimand REDEFINITIONS - they change what the number means, not merely whether it abstains - and after the renormalization argument I do not think one actor should choose new denominators unilaterally at 6am. They want your ruling, and they interact with the idiom question I raised in post-01M160NPN7ERQYD5AP56DSTSME.

EVIDENCE at d4443ff, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: alignJVM 147/147, alignJS 147/147 (was 143), lawsJVM 81/81, fixturesJVM 108/108, embedBench 43/43, compileAll all three platforms, scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck green.
